text:
maya: FYI alert — unexpected GPU billing jump in us-west1 overnight (~$11.6k). Cloud billing shows a sudden fleet of machines launched by the autoscaler.

sachin: any idea which machines? sounds like the autoscaler picked the wrong instance template again?

maya: digging. quick grep of GCE activity -> lots of `n1-standard-16` preemptibles created between 02:10-02:40, but our desired template is `a2-highgpu-1g` (A100). numbers: 24 n1 vs expected 8 a2.

linh: that's odd — autoscaler should only pick GPU-capable templates. Is the instance_template reference wrong in the autoscaler resource? Could be a terraform var interpolation bug.

maya: exact repro from logs: autoscaler launched instance template id `it-2026-03-02-v3` which has machine_type: `n1-standard-16` and labels: {gpu: "false"}

devon: heads up: billing shows committed use discount not applied for those VMs — label mismatch on project tag means the CUD didn't attach. So twofold hit: wrong instance family + lost commitment.

billing-bot: automated note: CUD coverage dropped from 86% -> 42% for compute.googleapis.com in us-west1 during window 02:00-03:00.

sachin: could be the instance_template variable got overwritten by a merge commit that defaulted to `var.fallback_machine` when `var.gpu_enabled` is false. I remember a recent refactor to remove duplicate templates.

maya: found the tf change: commit 7f3a2c removed explicit `template_gpu = var.template_gpu ?? default` and now the module consumes `local.selected_template` which falls back incorrectly. Patch candidate in my branch.

linh: mitigation? drain and replace those n1 nodes.

devon: I'm running `gcloud compute instances list --filter='name~"autosc-.*" AND zone:(us-west1-*)' --format='csv(name,machineType,status,labels)'` and will kick a drain + delete for the preemptible ones. Plan: cordon + live migrate pods where possible, then delete.

ops-bot: deploy bot: triggered rollout of fix branch `infra/fix-instance-select` to staging. Will apply to prod after approval.

maya: also opened billing ticket referencing charge IDs. @billing-bot please escalate CUD attribution; we need retroactive coverage if possible.

billing-bot: filed support case #CLOUD-77281 with vendor. Provided timestamps and example instance IDs.

sachin: postmortem action items: (1) add CI check to validate instance_template.gpu label matches autoscaler expectation, (2) revert the fallback behavior, (3) add alert if CUD coverage drops >10% in region, (4) run a nightly diff of active instance templates vs desired catalog.

devon: started remediation at 03:05 — drained 18/24 n1 nodes, deleted 14. Autoscaler config patched to pin template by template_id instead of var name.

maya: thanks. keep updates here. once we have final cost delta and root cause, we'll do follow-up with finance.

linh: small note — please avoid changing default fallback values in infra modules without a feature flag. :pray:

maya: agreed. I'll send the PR to revert and add a test. closing after billing response and cost reconciliation.

ops-bot: incident severity: S2. Labels: cost, autoscaler, billing.
